title: CHAPTER TWENTY-EIGHT. On the mode of production, parts, marriage, possession, and chief dignity of humankind
latin: CAPUT VIGESIMUM OCTAVUM, De modo productionis, partibus, conjugio, possessione et praecipua dignitate HOMINIS. Hactenus de ore hominis, quantum ad suum principium, Deum videlicet, cujus essentiam, subsistentiam, sufficientiam et efficientiam varie expendimus: sequitur MODUS quo homo ortus est, qui est productio illius e rubra terra cum afflatu spiritaculi vitae ad imaginem et similitudinem creatoris. Homo, ut fuit ultima creaturarum, ita et creaturarum omnium tam immediate quam mediate perfectarum compendium fuit, participans illarum naturam quantum ad spiritum, harum vero quantum ad corpus: mundi epitome, temporis et aeternitatis horizon. Fuit insuper etiam mediate perfectarum finis, et propterea in illis et supra illas quantum ad intentionem creatoris spectatus. Idcirco alio modo creatus dicitur quam caeterae creaturae. Nam illae per solum verbum productae fuerunt: Esto lux, esto expansum, etc.; homo vero quasi consilio ac deliberatione majore: Faciamus hominem — Gen. I.26 — cujus imaginis rationem nobis declarant 1. Natura Christi humana, quia pura erat et integra, qualis in Adamo ante lapsum; 2. Natura humana in caelo glorificata; 3. Universale peccatum, quia in locum hujus imaginis amissae successit; 4. Renovatio inchoata, quia per eam in nobis incipit restitui — Col. III.10; Ephes. IV.24.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): because through it it begins to be restored in us — Colossians 3:10; Ephesians 4:24 — (4) begun renovation. because it succeeded into ye place belonging toward this lost image — (3) universal sin. (2) human nature glorified in heaven. because it was pure plus whole such as in Adam before ye fall — (1) ye human nature belonging toward Christ — whose reason belonging toward image they declare toward us. Let us make humankind — Genesis 1:26 — but humankind as if by greater counsel plus deliberation. Let there be light, let there be expanse, etc. — for those were produced through ye Word alone. therefore he is said to have been created in another mode than ye other creatures. plus on that account viewed in them plus above them with respect toward ye intention belonging toward ye creator. He was moreover also ye end belonging toward those mediately perfect. ye epitome belonging toward ye world, ye horizon belonging toward time plus eternity — participating their nature with respect toward spirit but these with respect toward body. thus also he was ye compendium belonging toward all creatures both immediately plus mediately perfect. Humankind as he was ye last belonging toward creatures. which is ye production belonging toward him out from red earth with ye breath belonging toward ye spiritacle belonging toward life toward ye image plus likeness belonging toward ye creator — there follows ye MODE by which humankind arose. whose essence, subsistence, sufficiency, plus efficiency we have variously weighed — thus far concerning ye origin belonging toward humankind as far as toward his principle namely God. On ye mode belonging toward production, parts, marriage, possession, plus chief dignity belonging toward HUMANKIND. CHAPTER TWENTY-EIGHT.
english: CHAPTER TWENTY-EIGHT. On the mode of production, parts, marriage, possession, and chief dignity of humankind.

Thus far concerning the origin of humankind as far as concerns his principle, namely God, whose essence, subsistence, sufficiency, and efficiency we have variously weighed: there follows the MODE by which humankind arose, which is his production from red earth with the breath of the spirit of life according to the image and likeness of the Creator.

Humankind, as he was the last of creatures, was also the compendium of all creatures both immediately and mediately perfect, participating their nature as to spirit and these as to body: the epitome of the world, the horizon of time and eternity. He was moreover also the end of those mediately perfect, and therefore viewed in them and above them with respect to the Creator's intention. Therefore he is said to have been created in another mode than the other creatures. For those were produced by the Word alone: Let there be light, let there be an expanse, and so on; but humankind as if by greater counsel and deliberation: Let us make humankind — Genesis 1:26 — whose image's reason is declared to us by (1) Christ's human nature, pure and whole as in Adam before the fall; (2) human nature glorified in heaven; (3) universal sin, which succeeded into the place of this lost image; (4) begun renovation, by which it begins to be restored in us — Colossians 3:10; Ephesians 4:24.

title: II–VII: definition; essential parts — body and rational immortal spirit
latin: II. Homo est creaturarum ultima a DEO λόγῳ facta de pulvere terrae, sufflatuque in nares ipsius facta anima vivens, spiritu rationali immortali praedita ad imaginem Dei secundum similitudinem ipsius. Breviter quidem et philosophico more finitur homo animal rationale; nos hic eum in ordine ad creationem suam considerantes descripsimus e textu biblico Gen. I.26–27; IX.6; Eccl. VII.29; Act. XVII.28; 1 Cor. XI.7. III. Sunt autem in homine considerandae tum partes essentiales, tum sexus, tum denique affectiones propriae. IV. Ejus partes essentiales sunt corpus animatum et spiritus rationalis. V. CORPUS humanum est pars illius visibilis, structura carnea, ossibus fulta et cute contecta, sufflatu animata — Gen. II.7; Job. X.11; Matth. VI.25; 1 Cor. XII.12. VI. SPIRITUS rationalis et immortalis est pars hominis invisibilis, intellectu et voluntate pollens, corpori humano ita unitus ut tamen ab eo separari possit — Gen. II.7; Zach. XII.1; Matth. X.28; Act. VII.59; 2 Cor. V; XII.2; 1 Thess. V.23; Apoc. VI.9. VII. Hic spiritus, quamvis in corpore habitet, per se tamen est essentia corporis expers.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): yet through himself he is an essence lacking body — although this spirit dwells in ye body. VII. Revelation 6:9 — 1 Thessalonians 5:23 — 2 Corinthians 5; 12:2 — Acts 7:59 — Matthew 10:28 — Zechariah 12:1 — Genesis 2:7 — powerful with intellect plus will, so united toward ye human body that nevertheless he can be separated out from it — ye invisible part belonging toward humankind. VI. Ye rational plus immortal SPIRIT is. Genesis 2:7; Job 10:11; Matthew 6:25; 1 Corinthians 12:12 — a fleshy structure supported by bones plus covered by skin, animated by breath — ye visible part belonging toward him. V. Ye human BODY is. IV. His essential parts are ye animated body plus ye rational spirit. III. But in humankind there are to be considered both essential parts, plus sex, plus finally proper affections. Acts 17:28; 1 Corinthians 11:7 — Ecclesiastes 7:29 — Genesis 1:26-27; 9:6 — we here considering him in order toward his creation have described him out from ye biblical text. briefly indeed plus in philosophical manner humankind is defined a rational animal. according toward His likeness toward ye image belonging toward God — endowed with immortal rational spirit — made a living soul by breath into his nostrils — made by GOD through ye Word out from ye dust belonging toward earth. II. Humankind is ye last belonging toward creatures.
english: II. Humankind is the last of creatures, made by GOD through the Word from the dust of the earth, and by breath into his nostrils made a living soul, endowed with immortal rational spirit according to the image of God after His likeness. Briefly and in the philosophical manner humankind is defined a rational animal; we here, considering him in order to his creation, have described him from the biblical text — Genesis 1:26–27; 9:6; Ecclesiastes 7:29; Acts 17:28; 1 Corinthians 11:7.

III. In humankind there are to be considered essential parts, sex, and finally proper affections. IV. His essential parts are the animated body and the rational spirit. V. The human BODY is his visible part, a fleshy structure supported by bones and covered by skin, animated by breath — Genesis 2:7; Job 10:11; Matthew 6:25; 1 Corinthians 12:12. VI. The rational and immortal SPIRIT is the invisible part of humankind, powerful with intellect and will, so united to the human body that nevertheless it can be separated from it — Genesis 2:7; Zechariah 12:1; Matthew 10:28; Acts 7:59; 2 Corinthians 5; 12:2; 1 Thessalonians 5:23; Revelation 6:9. VII. This spirit, though it dwells in the body, is through itself an essence without body.

title: Mind above elements; intellect, will, executive power
latin: Credimus bene formato corpori et anima vivente, quam cum omnibus piscibus et avibus diei quinti animalibusque terrenis diei sexti homo communem habet — Gen. I.20 et 30 — exornato copulari mentem a Deo immissam, quam nos vegetante et sentiente diviniorem esse his RATIONIBUS confirmamus. 1. Quia nullus effectus elevatur supra causam suam principalem et adaequatam. Ergo anima humana spiritu sentiente reipsa divinior. Mens humana tam intelligendo quam appetendo supra solem et caelum caelorum et mundos quamvis plurimos cogitat, et intelligit semper aliquid ultra ea quae scit in infinitum. Ex quo conficimus eam non esse effectum solis et elementorum, ut spiritus sensitivus, sed prolem Infiniti quem Deum dicimus. VIII. Animae rationalis facultates sunt. IX. Intellectus est facultas animae qua objecta sub ratione veri apprehendimus, discernimus, et vel approbamus vel improbamus — theoreticus et practicus; hic συντήρησις et συνείδησις, i.e. observatio et conscientia. Vide Amesium L.1 de conscientia. X. Voluntas est facultas animae rationalis quae objecta sub ratione boni appetit et mali aversatur. Hujus facultatis natura est non cogi, et secundum naturae suae primam institutionem nulla necessitate ad extrema restringi. XI. Potentia exsecutrix est facultas animae qua objecta practica efficimus vel impedimus vel saltem permittimus.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): by which we effect or impede or at least permit practical objects — XI. Ye executive power is ye faculty belonging toward ye soul. plus according toward ye first institution belonging toward its nature to be restricted by no necessity toward extremes — ye nature belonging toward this faculty is not to be compelled. which seeks objects under ye reason belonging toward good plus turns away out from evil. X. Will is ye faculty belonging toward ye rational soul. see Ames Book 1 on conscience — here observation plus conscience. theoretical plus practical — by which we apprehend, discern, plus either approve or disapprove objects under ye reason belonging toward truth. IX. Intellect is ye faculty belonging toward ye soul. VIII. Ye faculties belonging toward ye rational soul are. but ye offspring belonging toward ye Infinite whom we call God — out from which we conclude that it is not an effect belonging toward sun plus elements as ye sensitive spirit. plus always understands something beyond those things which it knows into infinity — ye human mind both by understanding plus by seeking thinks above ye sun plus ye heaven belonging toward heavens plus worlds however many. therefore ye human soul is in reality more divine than ye sensing spirit. because no effect is elevated above its principal plus adequate cause. (1) which we confirm by these REASONS to be more divine than ye vegetative plus sensing. we believe that toward ye well-formed body plus living soul which humankind has in common with all fishes plus birds belonging toward ye fifth day plus terrestrial animals belonging toward ye sixth day — Genesis 1:20 plus 30 — adorned, ye mind sent in by God is coupled.
english: We believe that to the well-formed body and living soul — which humankind has in common with all fishes and birds of the fifth day and terrestrial animals of the sixth, Genesis 1:20 and 30 — adorned, the mind sent in by God is coupled, which we confirm by these REASONS to be more divine than the vegetative and sensing soul. (1) Because no effect is elevated above its principal and adequate cause. Therefore the human soul is in reality more divine than the sensing spirit. The human mind, both by understanding and by seeking, thinks above the sun and the heaven of heavens and worlds however many, and always understands something beyond what it knows, into infinity. From which we conclude that it is not an effect of sun and elements, as the sensitive spirit is, but the offspring of the Infinite whom we call God.

VIII. The faculties of the rational soul are these. IX. Intellect is the faculty of the soul by which we apprehend, discern, and either approve or disapprove objects under the reason of truth — theoretical and practical; here observation and conscience. See Ames, Book 1 on conscience. X. Will is the faculty of the rational soul which seeks objects under the reason of good and turns from evil. The nature of this faculty is not to be compelled, and according to its first institution to be restricted by no necessity to extremes. XI. Executive power is the faculty of the soul by which we effect or impede or at least permit practical objects.

title: XII–XVI: sex; male and female; first parents Adam and Eve
latin: XII. Haec de partibus hominis essentialibus: sequitur sexus, quo organis generationis discretus posteris suis originem praebet. XIII. Estque homo secundum sexum mas et femina. Haec differentia sexus necessaria est generationi, adeoque ad perfectionem humani generis. Unumquodque enim ens tunc perfectum dicitur in physicis, cum sibi simile generare potest. Quare cum solus mas generare nequeat, non omnino perfectus censetur ad consummationem sui generis, nisi et alteram sui portionem habeat. Eapropter Christus Matth. XIX.4 laudans textum Mosis ait: Non legistis opificem ab initio fecisse masculum et feminam. Et Moses Gen. II.18: Non est bonum hominem esse solum; faciam ei adjumentum quod sit coram eo. Et v.21–22 Dominus Deus arctissimo sopore consopivit Adamum et ex costis unam detraxit et construxit Deus ex ea costa mulierem. XIV. Sexus elucet tum in primis parentibus tum in posteris. XV. Primi parentes sunt primi homines. XVI. Adamus fuit primus vir, divinitus formatus; Eva prima femina e costa Adami constructa.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Eve ye first woman constructed out from ye rib belonging toward Adam — Adam was ye first man divinely formed. XVI. Ye first parents are ye first humans. XV. Sex shines forth both in ye first parents plus in descendants. XIV. plus verses 21-22 ye Lord God caused Adam to sleep with deepest sleep plus drew out one out from ye ribs plus constructed ye woman out from that rib. I will make toward him a help that is before him — Genesis 2:18 — And Moses: It is not good that ye human be alone. Have you not read that ye Maker from ye beginning made male plus female — Matthew 19:4 — on which account Christ praising Moses text says. unless he also have ye other portion belonging toward himself — therefore since ye male alone cannot generate he is not altogether judged perfect toward ye consummation belonging toward his genus. when it can generate ye like belonging toward itself — for each being is then called perfect in physics. This difference belonging toward sex is necessary toward generation plus thus toward ye perfection belonging toward ye human genus. XIII. Plus humankind according toward sex is male plus female. by which distinguished by ye organs belonging toward generation he furnishes origin toward his descendants — there follows sex. XII. These things concerning ye essential parts belonging toward humankind.
english: XII. So much concerning the essential parts of humankind: there follows sex, by which, distinguished by the organs of generation, he furnishes origin to his descendants. XIII. And humankind according to sex is male and female. This difference of sex is necessary for generation, and so for the perfection of the human race. For each being is then called perfect in physics when it can generate its like. Therefore, since the male alone cannot generate, he is not altogether judged perfect for the consummation of his genus unless he also have the other portion of himself. On that account Christ in Matthew 19:4, praising Moses' text, says: Have you not read that the Maker from the beginning made male and female? And Moses in Genesis 2:18: It is not good that the human be alone; I will make him a help that is before him. And in verses 21–22 the Lord God caused Adam to sleep with deepest sleep, drew out one of the ribs, and constructed the woman from that rib.

XIV. Sex shines forth both in the first parents and in their descendants. XV. The first parents are the first humans. XVI. Adam was the first man, divinely formed; Eve the first woman, constructed from Adam's rib.

title: XIX: marriage; paradise prepared for the first pair
latin: XIX. CONJUGIUM est foedus quo mas et femina in unam societatem vitae junguntur ad mutuum adjutorium, sobolis generationem et educationem, et castitatis conservationem. De conjugio Adami et Evae vide Zanchium de operibus Dei et alios. Hortus ille paradisi sic fuit paratus ut commodissime primis parentibus habitaretur: locus amoenus, arboribus vitae et scientiae boni et mali distinctus, fluviis irrigatus. Quod tamen paradisus non tam late patuerit quam totus orbis, nec sit ubique quaerendus allegoricis deliriumibus Origenistarum, tenendum est. Rejicienda sunt omnia illa quae paradisum aut mere allegoricum fingunt aut extra hanc terram collocant contra Mosis narrationem historicam Gen. II.8–15.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): against Moses historical narration Genesis 2:8-15 — which either invent paradise as merely allegorical or place it outside this earth — all those things are to be rejected. it is to be held that nevertheless paradise did not lie open so widely as ye whole world nor is to be sought everywhere by ye allegorical deliriums belonging toward ye Origenists. irrigated by rivers — distinguished by ye trees belonging toward life plus belonging toward ye knowledge belonging toward good plus evil — a pleasant place — so that it was most conveniently inhabited by ye first parents — that garden belonging toward paradise was thus prepared. see Zanchi on ye works belonging toward God plus others — concerning ye marriage belonging toward Adam plus Eve. toward mutual help, ye generation plus education belonging toward offspring, plus ye conservation belonging toward chastity — by which male plus female are joined into one society belonging toward life. XIX. MARRIAGE is ye covenant.
english: XIX. MARRIAGE is the covenant by which male and female are joined into one society of life for mutual help, the generation and education of offspring, and the conservation of chastity. Concerning the marriage of Adam and Eve see Zanchi on the works of God and others.

That garden of paradise was so prepared that it was most conveniently inhabited by the first parents: a pleasant place, distinguished by the trees of life and of the knowledge of good and evil, irrigated by rivers. Yet it is to be held that paradise did not lie open so widely as the whole world, nor is it to be sought everywhere by the allegorical deliriums of the Origenists. All those views are to be rejected which either invent paradise as merely allegorical or place it outside this earth against Moses' historical narration in Genesis 2:8–15.

title: Image and likeness of God in the whole human; natural and supernatural
latin: Sequitur hominis affectio, quae est quod totus et anima et corpore conditus est ad imaginem Dei et secundum similitudinem ejus, in quo summa ejus perfectio conspicitur. Differt quidem imago a similitudine ut species a genere; apud quosdam similitudo exegesis imaginis est, quasi dicatur imago Dei simillima — Gen. I.27; V.1. Vox imaginis significat vel ipsum ἀρχέτυπον ad cujus exemplar aliud fit, vel id quod ad aliud fit. Priore acceptione solus Christus imago Dei dici potest; posteriore in nulla re aspectabili praeterquam in homine imago Dei conspicitur. Nos vero asserimus subjectum illius primo ac per se esse animam rationalem, justitiae sanctitatis ac veritatis donis pulcherrime exornatam. Corpus vero humanum ab imaginis hujus ratione non prorsus excludimus. Recte igitur dicitur totus homo ad imaginem Dei conditus — id quod vel ex instauratione hujus imaginis liquet, in qua non tantum anima sed totus homo ipsumque adeo corpus ita instauratur ut sit templum Spiritus Sancti. Imago autem Dei non in viro tantum sed et in femina exstat, licet in viro sit illustrior.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): although in ye man it is more illustrious — but ye image belonging toward God exists not in ye man only but also in ye woman. so that it be ye temple belonging toward ye Holy Spirit — in which not only ye soul but ye whole human plus even ye body itself is so restored — which is clear even out from ye restoration belonging toward this image. therefore ye whole human is rightly said to have been created toward ye image belonging toward God. but we do not altogether exclude ye human body out from ye reason belonging toward this image. most beautifully adorned with ye gifts belonging toward justice, holiness, plus truth — but we assert that its subject first plus through itself is ye rational soul. ye image belonging toward God is beheld in no visible thing except in humankind — in ye latter acceptance. only Christ can be called ye image belonging toward God — in ye former acceptance. or that which is made toward another — it signifies either ye archetype itself toward whose exemplar another is made. ye voice belonging toward image. Genesis 1:27; 5:1 — among some likeness is ye exegesis belonging toward image as if it were said ye most similar image belonging toward God. image indeed differs out from likeness as species out from genus. in which his highest perfection is beheld — that ye whole both by soul plus by body was created toward ye image belonging toward God plus according toward His likeness. there follows ye affection belonging toward humankind which is.
english: There follows the affection of humankind, which is that the whole human, both by soul and by body, was created according to the image of God and after His likeness, in which his highest perfection is beheld. Image differs from likeness as species from genus; among some, likeness is the exegesis of image, as if it were said the most similar image of God — Genesis 1:27; 5:1.

The word image signifies either the archetype itself to whose exemplar another is made, or that which is made toward another. In the former acceptance only Christ can be called the image of God; in the latter, the image of God is beheld in no visible thing except in humankind. We assert that its subject first and through itself is the rational soul, most beautifully adorned with the gifts of justice, holiness, and truth. Yet we do not altogether exclude the human body from the reason of this image. Rightly, therefore, the whole human is said to have been created according to the image of God — which is clear even from the restoration of this image, in which not only the soul but the whole human, and even the body itself, is so restored as to be the temple of the Holy Spirit. And the image of God exists not in the man only but also in the woman, though in the man it is more illustrious.

title: Natural and supernatural parts of the image; Cap. 28 close toward governance
latin: Possunt autem istius imaginis partes sic distingui, ut aliae sint homini naturales, aliae supernaturales, aliae essentiales, aliae accidentales, aliae conveniant ei toti, aliae secundum aliquam partem — animam videlicet aut corpus. Animae naturale et essentiale est esse spiritum et praeditam facultate intelligendi et volendi tum secundum naturam tum secundum modum libertatis. Supernaturale vero et accidentale: notitia Dei rerumque ad salutem aeternam requisitarum, quae sapientiae nomine venit, et voluntatis secundum illam notitiam rectitudo et sanctitas. Immortalitas hactenus est animae essentialis ut mori nequeat nisi esse desinat; supernaturalis vero et accidentalis quatenus est ex gratia et assistentia conservationis. Corpori vero immortalitas tota est supernaturalis et accidentalis. Toti vero homini externe competit dominium in creaturas. Porro imago illa Dei quam homo in lapsu amisisse dicitur non fuit tota naturalis sed supernaturalis, peculiari Dei dono concessa — justitia, innocentia, integritas: in intellectu supernaturalis cognitio essentiae et voluntatis Dei; in voluntate summa ad bonum cognitum inclinatio seu summa erga Deum obedientia et subjectio; in appetitu summa cum ratione concordia. Finis denique propter quem ita homo conditus est, ut Deum creatorem suum agnosceret, diligeret, coleret et cum eo beatus in aeternum viveret — quo creationis actu Deus gloriam sapientiae, bonitatis et potentiae suae exhibuit clarissime.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): by which act belonging toward creation God most clearly exhibited ye glory belonging toward His wisdom, goodness, plus power — so that he would acknowledge, love, worship his Creator God plus live blessed with Him forever — finally ye end on account belonging toward which humankind was thus created. in ye appetite ye highest concord with reason — in ye will ye highest inclination toward known good or ye highest obedience plus subjection toward God — in ye intellect supernatural knowledge belonging toward ye essence plus will belonging toward God — justice, innocence, integrity — but was supernatural granted by ye peculiar gift belonging toward God. moreover that image belonging toward God which humankind is said to have lost in ye fall was not wholly natural. externally dominion over creatures belongs toward ye whole human. but toward ye body immortality is wholly supernatural plus accidental. but supernatural plus accidental insofar as it is out from grace plus ye assistance belonging toward conservation — immortality is thus far essential toward ye soul so that it cannot die unless it cease to be. plus ye rectitude plus holiness belonging toward ye will according toward that knowledge — ye knowledge belonging toward God plus belonging toward things required toward eternal salvation which comes by ye name belonging toward wisdom. but supernatural plus accidental. to be a spirit plus endowed with ye faculty belonging toward understanding plus willing both according toward nature plus according toward ye mode belonging toward freedom — what is natural plus essential toward ye soul. some agree toward him wholly, others according toward some part — namely soul or body — some essential, some accidental — some natural toward ye human, some supernatural. but ye parts belonging toward this image can be thus distinguished.
english: The parts of this image can be distinguished thus: some are natural to the human, some supernatural; some essential, some accidental; some belong to him wholly, others according to some part — namely soul or body. What is natural and essential to the soul is to be a spirit and endowed with the faculty of understanding and willing both according to nature and according to the mode of freedom. What is supernatural and accidental: the knowledge of God and of things required for eternal salvation, which comes under the name of wisdom, and the rectitude and holiness of the will according to that knowledge. Immortality is thus far essential to the soul that it cannot die unless it cease to be; but supernatural and accidental insofar as it is from grace and the assistance of conservation. To the body, immortality is wholly supernatural and accidental. To the whole human externally belongs dominion over creatures.

Moreover that image of God which humankind is said to have lost in the fall was not wholly natural but supernatural, granted by God's peculiar gift — justice, innocence, integrity: in the intellect, supernatural knowledge of God's essence and will; in the will, the highest inclination to known good, or the highest obedience and subjection toward God; in the appetite, the highest concord with reason. Finally the end for which humankind was thus created is that he would acknowledge, love, and worship his Creator God and live blessed with Him forever — by which act of creation God most clearly exhibited the glory of His wisdom, goodness, and power.
